note: Growth programs one level below the ten strategy families. `tin.coverage` says how much of the program Tin runs today: full (Tin does the work up to a founder review), partial (Tin does a named part), none (stays with the founder). `tin.workflows` are registry keys; the live runnable state per project comes from the plan run's `tin_state` input (system rows map to `system_*` run inputs via `input`), never from this file. `workflow_titles` maps every key to the title the founder sees in Tin; use titles in founder-facing text. `workflow_scope` is what each workflow actually does; never aim a workflow at work outside its scope. `rubric.json` and `score.py` rank these fifteen systems for a business; the plan never shows the profile or the scores. `tin.impact` is the share of a system's work Tin can carry today (0 to 1); the proposed scope and the levels order systems by fit × impact, the table by fit alone.

programs.name: Organic search content
programs.what: Editorial, comparison, alternative and answer pages that win the searches buyers already make.
fits_when: buyers search for the problem or the category by name
the site can take new pages
the founder can wait months for compounding traffic
weak_when: the category is too new to be searched
nobody can publish to the site

tin.founder_keeps: publishing to the site and the final voice
tin.impact_note: Tin researches, plans and drafts every piece; the founder publishes and keeps the voice.

programs.name: Technical SEO
programs.what: Site health: titles, descriptions, indexing, canonical tags, speed, broken pages.
fits_when: the site already gets impressions
pages ship with missing or duplicate metadata
the code lives on GitHub
weak_when: nobody can merge a pull request

tin.founder_keeps: merging and deploying the pull requests
tin.impact_note: Tin audits and opens the fix as a pull request; the founder merges.

programs.name: AI visibility
programs.what: Being found, cited and recommended when buyers ask AI assistants for tools and vendors.
fits_when: buyers ask assistants which tool to use
named competitors already come up in AI answers
the product has a clear category
weak_when: buying is local, offline or relationship-led

tin.impact_note: Tin measures weekly and drafts answer pages; being cited still depends on what gets published.

programs.name: Paid search
programs.what: Ads on buyer intent queries with conversion tracking.
fits_when: clear buyer queries exist
unit economics support a paid acquisition cost
there is a monthly budget
weak_when: long sales cycles with no lead capture

tin.founder_keeps: the budget, approving the exact campaign before it goes live, and any bidding or budget change Tin proposes
tin.impact_note: Tin assesses fit, launches one approved Google Search campaign in the founder's own account and checks it daily; the founder approves the plan and every budget or bidding change.

programs.name: Paid social
programs.what: Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn or YouTube ads with tested creative.
fits_when: the product shows well in a short video
consumer or prosumer buyers
there is a creative and media budget

tin.founder_keeps: campaigns, targeting and spend; Tin makes the creative
tin.impact_note: Tin makes the creative; targeting and spend stay with the founder.

programs.name: Cold outbound email
programs.what: Email sequences to a defined list of buyers, with follow-ups and reply handling.
fits_when: buyer roles and companies can be named
the deal size justifies a reply from the founder
a sender mailbox exists
weak_when: a price too low to justify replies

tin.founder_keeps: approving every send, replying, and any list beyond the connected inbox
tin.impact_note: Tin builds the list, drafts, sends after approval and follows up; the founder replies.

programs.name: Founder-led sales
programs.what: Warm follow-ups, demos, calls and closing done by the founder.
fits_when: deals are large enough for a call
agency, team or multi-tenant buyers
early stage with few customers
weak_when: pure self-serve at a low price

tin.founder_keeps: the calls and the close; Tin builds the warm list and researches accounts
tin.impact_note: Tin builds the warm list and researches accounts; the calls and the close are the founder's.

programs.name: Product-led growth
programs.what: A free path, fast activation, and loops inside the product that bring the next user.
fits_when: self-serve signup exists
time to value is minutes
usage-based or tiered pricing

tin.founder_keeps: product decisions and shipping; Tin finds the breaks and proposes bounded fixes
tin.impact_note: Tin finds the breaks and proposes bounded fixes; product decisions and shipping are the founder's.

programs.name: Conversion and trust
programs.what: Landing page clarity, proof, pricing page, and signup friction.
fits_when: traffic exists but signups are low
the hero does not name the buyer
the trial converts poorly
weak_when: there is no traffic to convert yet

tin.impact_note: Tin walks the signup and opens small fixes; copy and proof are the founder's.

programs.name: Owned audience
programs.what: Newsletter, changelog, lifecycle and win-back email to people who already opted in.
fits_when: a list or user base exists
releases ship on a cadence
retention matters more than reach

tin.founder_keeps: the list, the tool and the sends; Tin drafts
tin.impact_note: Tin drafts; the list, the tool and the sends are the founder's.

programs.name: Earned media and launches
programs.what: Launch posts, Show HN and Product Hunt, press, founder posts, short video.
fits_when: the product is novel or visual
the founder will post and reply in public
a community for the category exists

tin.founder_keeps: posting and engaging; Tin makes the article, video and figures
tin.impact_note: Tin makes the article, video and figures; posting and engaging are the founder's.

programs.name: Platform and marketplaces
programs.what: Listings where buyers already shop: integration directories, package registries, app stores, agent and tool registries.
fits_when: the product is an API, plugin or integration
the ecosystem has directories buyers browse
weak_when: a standalone consumer app with no ecosystem

tin.founder_keeps: accounts and submissions; Tin finds the directories and prepares listing copy
tin.impact_note: Tin maps the integrations to partner marketplaces and fills in the listing forms; accounts and submissions are the founder's.

programs.name: Community and events
programs.what: Meetups, Discord and Slack communities, hackathons, conferences.
fits_when: buyers gather in a few communities
the founder has hours to show up

tin.founder_keeps: showing up and pitching; Tin finds open calls and campus events and drafts the pitches
tin.impact_note: Tin finds open calls and events and drafts the pitches; showing up and sending are the founder's.

programs.name: Partnerships and channel
programs.what: Agencies, resellers, co-marketing and integration partners who bring their customers.
fits_when: agencies or multi-tenant buyers exist
complementary tools share the buyer
some proof exists to show a partner
weak_when: too early to show a partner anything

tin.impact_note: Tin researches and drafts the outreach; the terms and the relationship are the founder's.

programs.name: Pricing and packaging
programs.what: Tiers, trials, add-ons and packaging tests.
fits_when: conversion or expansion is the gap
enough volume to read a test
weak_when: too little volume to learn anything

tin.founder_keeps: the decision and the implementation; Tin watches competitors, reads who keeps paying and researches the options
tin.impact_note: Tin watches competitor pricing, reads who keeps paying and researches the options; the decision and the change are the founder's.

systems_checklist.ask: What is the site built with and where is it hosted?
Where does the site's code live, and which repository serves the site?
Which analytics tool records visits and signups (PostHog, GA4, Plausible, Mixpanel)?
systems_checklist.when: product analytics runs on PostHog Cloud

systems_checklist.ask: Is the site verified in Google Search Console, and under which account?
Which mailbox would send outreach and receive replies (Google Workspace, Gmail, Outlook)?
Where do leads and deals live, if anywhere?
Where do customers write when something breaks?
Where do the docs live, and can they be edited from the repository?
Which tool sends to the list, if there is one?
Which ad platforms have an account, and is anything running?

workflow_scope.brand.capture: Inspect a website and optional repository or source packet once. Propose missing BRAND.md and DESIGN.md together; one review adopts them. Existing documents stay unchanged. No source edits, automatic refresh or asset generation.
workflow_scope.content.deliver: Adapt an existing approved content.generate article to the connected website repository and open an unmerged PR. Requires source_run_id and expected_repository; no new drafting or implicit approval. Reuses the normal metered Codex procedure runner. Exact Markdown source preservation is checked; repository build and rendered equivalence are separate checks, never implied. CMS and WordPress publication require future connectors.
workflow_scope.organic.traffic_system: Audit your website and research buyer searches, then save an editable content plan to My system. Optionally propose one technical fix as an unmerged GitHub PR. Does not write articles, send outreach, merge or publish.
workflow_scope.style.capture: Use your coding agent to select writing samples, or add samples here. Save an editable voice guide for future content. Nothing is published.
workflow_scope.organic.technical_fix: Recheck one missing-title or missing-description finding and propose a verified PR. Supports exact static HTML and bounded Python-wheel HTML templates. Lists unsupported pages separately. If no safe repair is available, explain why without a PR. Never merges or deploys; GitHub may run its configured PR checks.
workflow_scope.content.plan: Turn an audit and keyword research into an editable two-week to six-month roadmap. Save to My system to prepare weekly batches. Does not write articles or publish.
workflow_scope.content.generate: Draft one selected brief from an initialized content program, using the project writing guide when available. Saves a separate reviewable Markdown draft with factual checks. Requires program_id; omit item_id to select the next eligible article, or select an explicit item through get_content_draft_sources. On demand only. Optional pinned repository delivery opens an unmerged PR only after article approval; otherwise use content.deliver for an approved source. Does not merge, publish, or change the roadmap.
workflow_scope.organic.keyword_plan: Research buyer searches, competitor keywords, and a bounded sample of Google results. Get an evidence-backed keyword inventory for content planning. No audit or GitHub required; does not create a calendar, write articles, or publish.
workflow_scope.organic.audit: Audit technical SEO and AI visibility (GEO). Check up to 100 public pages and see whether AI answers mention, cite, or recommend your business. Get a report, actionable findings, and supporting evidence. No GitHub required.
workflow_scope.content.design_md: Analyze a project repository and publish its DESIGN.md.
workflow_scope.project.memory: Consolidate durable project outputs into the project wiki.
workflow_scope.scan.report: Review durable project knowledge against the system scanning guide and publish SCAN.md.
workflow_scope.site.health_improve: Inspect one public site against its selected GitHub repository, make one bounded mechanical improvement, and open a pull request for review. When no safe change is justified, save a no-change report without opening a PR.
workflow_scope.visibility.audit: Measure whether Luna finds and recommends a chosen target across five target-blind buyer questions, then publish AI_VISIBILITY.md.
workflow_scope.content.answer_page: Create a public-facing Markdown content draft from the latest AI visibility findings; not for general advice or internal business questions.
workflow_scope.project.weekly_brief: Summarize what moved, what needs attention, and the smallest useful next steps from this project's durable week of activity.
workflow_scope.project.task: Use an isolated Codex task when the founder asks Tin to inspect, research, or change project files and no narrower registered workflow fits.
workflow_scope.research.deep_dive: Test a project question and its upstream assumptions against current, source-backed evidence.
workflow_scope.content.public_article: Turn durable project evidence and original thinking into a rigorous, reviewable public article.
workflow_scope.content.diagram: Turn a process or system into one clear Tin-styled diagram whose Mermaid source stays editable in project Files.
workflow_scope.outreach.email_shortlist: Review the connected Gmail and Calendar history to create a bounded, evidence-backed outreach shortlist in project Files.
workflow_scope.outreach.email_campaign: Snapshot selected shortlist recipients and exact email copy for approval, then send with reply-aware follow-up timers.
workflow_scope.qa.signup_walkthrough: Sign up for your product as a stranger with a Tin-owned test account, verify the email, reach first activation, and report every break along the way.
workflow_scope.product.code_map: Read the connected GitHub repository and write the Code map section of project memory: every user-facing surface with its exposure, plans and gating, integrations, and tech stack, each cited to file and line.
workflow_scope.product.deep_dive: Read the docs, sign in and use your product with a Tin-owned account, reconcile with the code map, and write the Feature map section of project memory with evidence on every feature.
workflow_scope.qa.product_audit: Exercise every feature in the project's Feature map as a user with a Tin-owned account and report what works, what is broken, and what to improve, with reproducible evidence.
workflow_scope.creative.character: Design a cute, on-brand vector mascot for the product as an animatable SVG character in project Files (three mouth shapes, a blink, and a payoff expression), ready to narrate demo videos and appear in marketing. Tin reads the product page and project memory itself and asks one model for the drawing; about two minutes, no sandbox.
workflow_scope.creative.product_demo: Capture the founder's live product at phone size and render a smooth 9:16 short-form demo video (TikTok, Reels, Shorts) with a pain hook, voiceover, word-synced captions, tap and scroll motion, and an optional narrating character from project Files.
workflow_scope.ads.assessment: Read the site, Keyword Planner, DataForSEO and Search Console when connected, then say whether Google Search ads fit: a verdict, the binding constraint, a scorecard and a rough campaign shape. Advisory; never creates or funds campaigns. On demand only.
workflow_scope.ads.launch: From a successful assessment, draft one Google Search campaign (keywords, ads, negatives, budget, click ceiling) for the founder's approval, then create it in their linked Google Ads account. Blocks until a conversion is measured; on demand only.
workflow_scope.ads.monitor: Read a launched campaign, add negatives from wasted search terms, pause disapproved ads and wasteful keywords, and propose budget or bidding changes for approval. Daily or weekly once a campaign is live.
workflow_scope.competitor.watch: Reread known competitors' public pricing and changelog pages weekly and report only material changes against the last watch, with at most three suggested Tin follow-ups. Never signs in, contacts competitors, publishes, or changes your pricing.
workflow_scope.qa.buyer_trust: Check the public site and checkout a buyer sees against fixed trust rules (HTTPS, security headers, exposed files, privacy, contact, refund and total-before-pay) and hand each code fix to Improve site health and each policy or host fix to the founder; public GET requests only, never signs in, submits forms, changes the site or claims CVE coverage.
workflow_scope.organic.mention_backlinks: Finds pages and AI-cited sources that name the product without linking to its site and drafts one ask per page for the founder to send; it never sends, contacts anyone or re-asks a page asked before.
workflow_scope.organic.error_surface: Reads the connected repository for user-visible error messages and ranks the undocumented ones as pages to add to content.plan as a context file, with cause and fix cited to code; it never writes pages, opens PRs or estimates demand.
workflow_scope.outreach.paying_segment: Reads Stripe subscriptions (the Stripe connection, a read-only restricted key) and names the customer segment that keeps paying, with exact inputs for the outreach shortlist, keyword plan and ads assessment; read-only, no model calls, never starts workflows or writes to Stripe.
workflow_scope.outreach.campus_events: For businesses whose buyers are students, finds or compares upcoming campus events, ranks them on cited evidence and drafts one permission-dependent activation; never contacts organizers or students, registers, pays or collects student data.
workflow_scope.outreach.speaking_shortlist: Find conferences, meetups and podcasts with an open call that fit the business, verify deadlines and requirements, and draft one pitch per venue; skips venues pitched before; never submits, applies or emails.
workflow_scope.outreach.syllabus_placement: Find public courses where students do the product's job, rank them by when instructors pick tools, and draft a teaching kit and notes; never guesses addresses, contacts anyone or promises offers.
workflow_scope.outreach.marketplace_listings: Map the Code map's integrations to partner app marketplaces, check presence and listing rules, and fill in the forms for up to three listings to submit; needs the Code map first; never repeats a prepared listing, signs up or submits.
workflow_scope.content.release_announce: Drafts an X post, LinkedIn post and newsletter email from one release's changelog, announcing only listed changes; never posts, sends or adds claims or links beyond the changelog and release link.
workflow_scope.growth.score_quiz: Drafts a self-contained scored quiz widget (a lead magnet) with a call to action to the founder's signup link; never deploys it, adds other links, or runs model-written code.
workflow_scope.product.analytics_brief: A recurring PostHog brief (needs the PostHog connection, read-only OAuth to one project): ordered activation, event trends, traffic, error signals and one supported breakdown with reproducible queries; read-only reporting, no product changes.
